decisions.approvalNote: User approved Option A and clarified that the guided experience should reuse the established ordered-steps visual pattern from Dataset Preparation and Model Training, with plain-language primary steps and progressive disclosure for advanced controls.
decisions.context: The choice determines whether the roadmap primarily reorganizes the user experience around a guided outcome, preserves the current technical forms, or exposes a configurable data-engineering pipeline. All options include the immediate correctness, compatibility, privacy, split-integrity, and diagnostic fixes; they differ in product structure, terminology, flexibility, and implementation scope.

consequences: Users choose goals and see readiness, warnings, samples, and recommended actions instead of configuring data-engineering internals first.
The system can enforce one end-to-end capability contract and refuse misleading format, split, or destination choices before work starts.
Dataset versions, quality reports, lineage, and publication documentation become normal outputs rather than optional expert tasks.
The roadmap is a larger modernization, delivered through a few independently useful increments with compatibility-preserving rollback.
options.label: Option A — Guided data workflow
options.summary: Create one plain-language journey—Add data, Check data, Prepare dataset, Review, and Publish—using sensible defaults, short explanations, previews, and an Advanced settings disclosure for technical controls. Preserve the accepted artifact/runtime architecture underneath, use a canonical streaming tabular representation for preparation, and make remote localization, profiling, curation, splitting, versioning, and dataset documentation part of the guided path.
tradeoffs: Best fit for non-technical users and the clearest way to prevent unsupported or unsafe combinations.
Requires coordinated contract, application, storage/provider, Python worker, desktop/thin-client, documentation, migration, and test work.
Advanced users retain detailed controls, but those controls move out of the primary path and may be grouped or renamed.

consequences: Correctness and security improve, but the product remains oriented toward technically experienced users.
Future features are likely to add more controls to already dense tabs.
A later UX restructuring would revisit many of the same components and tests.
options.label: Option B — Harden the existing tabs
options.summary: Keep the current Ingestion and Dataset Preparation forms and navigation, correct the split and format defects, add missing validation and quality controls, and improve labels/tooltips without materially changing the workflow structure.
tradeoffs: Smaller initial UI disruption and easier visual regression review.
Retains a long configuration form and makes users understand normalization, chunking, generation, split, format, and model controls before they can produce a dataset.
Quality review and publishing remain separate collections of controls rather than a guided outcome.

consequences: The Data Management area becomes a general data-orchestration product rather than a focused training-dataset workflow.
New persisted recipe, compatibility, execution-planning, versioning, and possibly distributed scheduling decisions would be required.
Delivery would take more increments and broaden beyond the current accepted runtime lifecycle constraints.
options.label: Option C — Visual pipeline builder
options.summary: Expose ingestion, normalization, profiling, filtering, generation, validation, splitting, and publication as user-configurable pipeline stages with reusable recipes and a graph or stage editor.
tradeoffs: Maximum flexibility, inspection, and extensibility for data engineers and research teams.
Highest implementation, migration, documentation, support, and accessibility cost.
Introduces substantial concepts and terminology that conflict with the requested non-technical default experience unless paired with a separate simplified mode.

decisions.title: Data Management workflow shape

constraints: Preserve the accepted staged-artifact model and the distinction between internal artifact identity, local object storage, and remote repository backing.
Keep business rules in domain/application layers, runtime parsing and model execution in adapters, host selection in composition, and renderer behavior behind typed clients.
Provide one guided default path using plain user language and progressive disclosure; keep model, parsing, generation, and performance tuning under clearly labeled advanced settings.
Do not show an input format, task, split, or destination as available unless the complete selected path is supported and covered by an end-to-end test.
Retain explicit workspace and organization context through contracts, transports, use cases, storage, runtime tasks, outputs, and publication; UI selection is not authorization.
Never put source content, prompts, model output, credentials, provider payloads, local paths, or raw logs into diagnostics, roadmap evidence, or public errors.
Pin external dataset inputs to immutable revisions or content digests and preserve lineage through normalization, curation, generation, splitting, and publication.
Bound file and batch counts, bytes, memory, concurrency, redirects, retries, runtime duration, generated rows, warning volume, previews, and retained reports.
Keep contextual errors and required decisions near the affected step while using the global notification center only for bounded cross-page outcomes and long-running activity.

Stay within the implemented Python sidecar and task-registry topology; generalized distributed execution, hybrid synchronization, encryption-at-rest policy, and public marketplace behavior require successor decisions.
Run focused tests for internal chunks and reserve the applicable documentation, architecture, agent-support, server, thin-client, desktop, and full-suite gates for each completed increment.

abuseCases: Malformed, deceptive, oversized, deeply nested, or unsupported inputs consume resources or bypass validation.
A remote URL, redirect, or provider object reaches a private network target, leaks credentials, or substitutes mutable content.
An artifact, task, preview, report, or published dataset crosses workspace or organization boundaries.
Source text, prompts, generated content, credentials, paths, provider payloads, or raw logs escape through diagnostics or UI messages.
Duplicate or related records cross data splits, evaluation data enters training, or reported split counts differ from materialized outputs.
PII, secrets, disallowed content, unlicensed material, or benchmark data is admitted without a visible policy decision.
Synthetic examples are hallucinated, mislabeled, low-quality, or accepted without grounding and review evidence.
Cancellation, cleanup, migration, compatibility, or rollback leaves partial outputs, orphaned data, or a less secure path.
assets: User-provided and remotely acquired documents, images, structured rows, annotations, and generated examples
Workspace and organization ownership, authorization context, and storage isolation
Hugging Face credentials, immutable source revisions, licenses, consent, and provenance records
Accurate schema, quality, deduplication, split, leakage, and publication results
Bounded host, network, storage, memory, GPU, and runtime resources
Sanitized diagnostics, previews, reports, notifications, and dataset documentation
controls: Retain existing upload classification, authorization, workspace-scoped storage, secure-egress, credential, and authenticated sidecar controls.
Create one capability registry that drives accepted inputs, UI choices, preparation paths, preview support, and output support.
Use immutable provider revisions or content digests, content-addressed lineage, bounded streaming, deterministic stage manifests, and atomic finalization.
Add explicit schema, quality, deduplication, language, PII/secret, license-policy, unsafe-content, contamination, and split-integrity gates with quarantine rather than silent loss.
Use bounded sanitized diagnostics and aggregate metrics only; never log or publicly return protected content.
Require authoritative workspace and organization context at every data, task, preview, and publication boundary and fail closed when it is missing or ambiguous.
Gate model-generated examples through structured validation, grounding checks, quality thresholds, and human review for uncertain samples.
Keep rollback additive and non-destructive, preserve immutable raw artifacts, and prevent fallback to unsupported, unscoped, mutable, or disclosure-prone behavior.
residualRisks: Automated PII, license, toxicity, contamination, quality, and synthetic-grounding checks can produce false positives and false negatives; organizations retain responsibility for policy and legal review.
OCR, semantic parsing, embedding-based deduplication, and model-assisted review may require optional dependencies and controlled hardware qualification before broad support.
Encryption at rest, hybrid synchronization, managed retention objectives, and generalized distributed execution remain outside this roadmap unless separately decided.
Physical accessibility and representative non-technical usability qualification require controlled human review in addition to local automated evidence.

discovery.summary: Data Ingestion has a sound staged-artifact, workspace, upload-validation, secure-egress, and provenance foundation, while Dataset Preparation has broad task and output coverage. The current end-to-end experience is not yet production-trustworthy: requested train/test ratios do not produce separate splits, the UI advertises input formats the worker cannot read, Hugging Face imports are remote Parquet registrations that require a separate localization step even though preparation cannot parse Parquet input, worker warnings are not surfaced, generation failures can log protected content, and the product lacks profiling, deduplication, privacy/license checks, leakage controls, human review, and versioned dataset documentation. The preparation form also exposes many model and data-engineering controls by default, which creates avoidable cognitive load for non-technical users.

Configured train, validation, and test ratios produce physically represented deterministic splits whose row counts match the result, whose groups or source documents do not cross boundaries, and whose exact duplicates cannot appear in more than one split.

Desktop and thin client use the established numbered WorkflowSequence and WorkflowStep presentation, show only goal-oriented primary controls and recommended defaults, place technical tuning under Advanced settings, preserve keyboard and screen-reader semantics, and remain usable at supported zoom and narrow widths.

Preparation warnings, skipped items, split counts, readiness problems, and result locations appear in bounded plain language with contextual correction or retry actions; the global notification center is used only for cross-page outcomes and authoritative long-running progress.

Upload, network, provider, storage, runtime, workspace, organization, and diagnostic boundaries remain fail closed and bounded; focused negative tests prove source content, prompts, model output, credentials, provider payloads, local paths, raw logs, and cross-workspace records cannot enter public diagnostics or the wrong workspace.

Controlled keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, and representative non-technical usability review confirms that users can add supported data, understand readiness, create a dataset, and find its result without opening Advanced settings or needing unexplained technical terms.

Python generation diagnostics currently include source text, prompts, and generated output; errors must retain bounded counts and reason codes while excluding protected content, provider payloads, model output, credentials, and host paths.
Moving technical controls under Advanced settings can break saved settings or tests unless state and request shapes remain backward compatible.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Enabled token, sentence, section, table, semantic, OCR, or layout processing preserves source artifact and bounded span or region lineage, emits measurable extraction quality, respects page, pixel, token, memory, and duration limits, and reports unsupported or low-confidence content without fabricating text.

Semantic duplicate detection, data mixing, balancing, coverage, and hard-negative recommendations are reproducible from recorded models and thresholds, preserve reviewable examples and metrics, prevent known cross-split leakage, and demonstrate improvement on approved synthetic reference datasets.

Generated candidates must pass task schema, grounding or source-support, duplication, quality, safety, and diversity checks; uncertain or rejected candidates enter quarantine with bounded reasons, and no model-generated row reaches an approved split without the configured review policy.

Users who do not enable advanced capabilities see the same concise ordered workflow and recommended defaults; users who opt in receive simple presets, readiness and time guidance, cancel and retry controls, and plain explanations while model, device, precision, threshold, and algorithm settings remain under Advanced settings.

Model outputs, OCR text, embeddings, prompts, citations, critic evidence, and rejected candidates remain workspace scoped, bounded, sanitized, and absent from diagnostics; unavailable capabilities, dependency failure, model failure, cancellation, and cleanup fail closed without admitting unverified rows or weakening baseline controls.

Controlled representative hardware and accessibility qualification proves OCR and layout extraction, semantic deduplication, hard-negative mining, model generation and criticism, progress, cancellation, memory and time bounds, quality evidence, and non-technical preset usability with synthetic data.
